svg.title: Which defects are the press's, and which came in the box
svg.desc: Insert-molding defects sorted into two columns. Fixable at the press: a weak bond with resin left on the metal points to infiltration, so raise mold temperature, injection speed and packing; sink and flow marks around the insert mean a cold insert chilling the melt, so raise mold temperature and preheat the insert; a weld line landing on the joint is moved with a gate change. Send back upstream: a weak bond that separates to bare clean metal is a treatment or handling failure; flash points to insert dimensions or a damaged shut-off; an insert that shifts or deforms is a fixturing problem. The fracture face decides the first split: resin on the metal is the press's problem, bare metal is the box's. A part that must seal is proven with a leak test, not a pull test.
svg.text: Read the defect back to its cause

g.text: Weak bond, resin left on the metal
infiltration — raise mold temp, speed, packing
the surface was good; you did not fill it
Sink & flow marks around the insert
raise mold temp, preheat the insert
Weld line landing on the joint
two flow fronts meeting at the interface
move it with a gate change
never wet in — do not mold through it

svg.text: The fracture face decides the split: resin on the metal is yours; bare metal came in the box.
And if the part must seal, prove it with a leak test, not a pull test — a seal does not average.
